chunks: And Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever reaches the standing at Jam‘ on the Day of Sacrifice before the sun passes its zenith has indeed attained hajj (pilgrimage)."

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ ٱلْحَجَّ: has attained or validly caught the hajj
key_terms.تَزُولَ ٱلشَّمْسُ: the sun passes its zenith, meaning midday begins to decline
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلنَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice during hajj rites
key_terms.ٱلْمَوْقِفَ: the standing place or ritual station meant here in the hajj rite

ai.seo_question: Until what time on the Day of Sacrifice can a pilgrim reach Jam‘ and still have attained hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the time limit for attaining hajj (pilgrimage). It indicates that if a person reaches the standing at Jam‘, meaning Muzdalifah, on the Day of Sacrifice before midday, their hajj is considered attained.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2774 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"Whoever reaches the standing at Muzdalifah (Jam‘) on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) before the sun passes its zenith has indeed attained Hajj."
